verdict: All five confirmed code defects fixed and regression-verified. The missing-encryption-key limitation for some view-once media remains.

checks.productionWorkerIsolation: Live production worker PID 635937 survived the full suite before the intentional deployment restart.

findings.title: Settings import accepts admin-controlled account properties
findings.evidence: Isolated import changed rentalExpiresAt to a caller-selected value. POST /api/backup/import requires an authenticated user but does not require admin. importUser uses a short denylist rather than an allowlist.
findings.impact: A user can extend their own rental period or change other account properties that should be managed by the platform admin.
findings.recommendation: Allowlist editable user settings and validate their types; reject rental, role, lifecycle, and account-control properties.
findings.resolution: Validated allowlist replaces arbitrary account-property import; protected rental, role, lifecycle and secret fields cannot be changed. Invalid settings are rejected before applying changes.

findings.title: Starting any manager kills all matching worker processes
findings.evidence: Startup executes pkill -f "bot_worker\.js" without a session-directory or parent-process boundary. Test suites start separate managers on isolated ports and session directories. Live logs contain worker shutdown/restart events during such test runs.
findings.impact: An isolated test manager or another installation can interrupt production WhatsApp workers and trigger reconnects.
findings.recommendation: Track and clean up only workers belonging to the same installation and session directory; avoid global process-name sweeps.
findings.resolution: Worker cleanup checks the Node executable, exact worker script, canonical session directory, user ID and optional exact account. Global pkill sweeps removed. Production worker remained alive throughout the full isolated-manager test suite.

findings.title: Admin bootstrap can throw before database queues are initialized
findings.evidence: With a temporary users.json containing a non-admin Alice and ADMIN_USERNAMES=alice, requiring lib/db.js exits with ReferenceError: Cannot access saveQueue before initialization.
findings.impact: A restart with newly configured admin promotions can fail during module initialization.
findings.recommendation: Initialize write queues before calling syncAdminUsers; add a startup regression test covering a newly promoted admin.
findings.resolution: Database queues are initialized before admin bootstrap. A normal-process test verifies first-time promotion and persistence.

findings.title: Backup archive omits key material and application settings
findings.evidence: A synthetic source containing creds.json, pre-key-1.json, sender-key-1.json, recovery-cache.json and session/app_settings.json produced an archive containing only creds.json and recovery-cache.json. The script matches prekeys-*.json rather than pre-key-*.json and has no sender-key/app_settings inclusion. SESSION_DIR overrides are also ignored.
findings.impact: Restoration can omit encryption state and saved administrator settings; custom session-directory deployments may back up the wrong directory.
findings.recommendation: Back up the actual configured session directory comprehensively and verify restoration into an isolated installation.
findings.resolution: Backup includes the complete configured session tree, follows a symlink directory, omits the live manager lock, refuses missing/nested destinations and uses a private archive. Synthetic backup/restore verifies key material, settings and login-session files.

findings.title: Saved-only Groq keys are not read by normal app entry points
findings.evidence: getGroqApiKey references fs and path without importing them. A normal temporary .cjs entry with only session/app_settings.json configured reports configured=false; the exception is silently swallowed. This can be hidden by node -e, where fs/path are available as globals.
findings.impact: A Groq key saved through the admin interface can stop being recognized after a full manager restart when it is absent from the environment.
findings.recommendation: Import fs/path explicitly and test stored-key loading from a normal CommonJS entry file.
findings.resolution: fs/path are explicitly imported. Stored-only Groq key loading is verified from a normal CommonJS process; startup key detection now uses the same resolver.

findings.title: .vv remains unavailable for the tested messages without encryption metadata
findings.evidence: Live attempts had no mediaKey, URL, directPath or cached original. Both primary-phone address variants failed to return a recoverable original.
findings.impact: Passing media tests does not establish that .vv works for all view-once posts.
findings.recommendation: Document the limitation accurately; require a usable original rather than claiming recovery of absent encryption data.

verificationLimits: Review and existing tests are not exhaustive proof of every live WhatsApp command.
Actual payment processing and every group moderation action were not exercised.
Reproductions used temporary fixtures; no credentials or real message content are included in this report.
Five code defects fixed and deployed; no claim that encryption metadata withheld by WhatsApp can be recovered.
